sections.purpose: To sterilize pharmaceutical preparations, glassware, and equipment using saturated steam under pressure as per pharmacopeial and cGMP requirements.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for sterilization of all materials requiring moist heat sterilization, including parenteral preparations, culture media, and labware.
procedure: Inspect the autoclave chamber, door gasket, pressure gauge, and safety valve for any damage before operation.
Fill the inner chamber with distilled water to the recommended level (usually up to the lower basket level — not above).
Load the materials to be sterilized: wrap glassware in aluminium foil; pack media/preparations in sealed containers; do not overfill the chamber.
Ensure all items are loosely packed to allow steam penetration to all surfaces.
Do not mix liquids and dry goods in the same sterilization cycle.
Close the autoclave door firmly and secure the locking mechanism.
Select the appropriate sterilization cycle: Standard cycle — 121°C, 15 psi (103 kPa), 15–20 minutes for most pharmaceutical materials.
Start the cycle: the autoclave will first exhaust air from the chamber (if vacuum-assisted) or vent steam through the air exhaust valve.
Monitor the temperature and pressure gauges to confirm the set point is reached.
Maintain sterilization conditions for the full required time after the set temperature is achieved.
After the hold time, allow pressure to fall naturally — do not force-open the door while pressure is above zero.
After pressure reaches zero and temperature drops to 80–90°C, open the door slightly (5 cm) and allow steam to escape for 5 minutes.
Using heat-resistant gloves and tongs, remove sterilized items carefully.
Allow items to cool before handling; check biological indicators or chemical indicators placed inside the load.
Record cycle details in the autoclave logbook: date, operator, cycle parameters, load description, indicator result.
Clean the chamber interior monthly or as per schedule using an approved cleaner.
precautions: Never open the autoclave door while pressure is above zero — risk of severe steam burns.
Do not overload the autoclave chamber — proper steam circulation is essential for sterilization.
Never autoclave materials sealed in non-autoclavable plastics or airtight metal containers.
Use appropriate wrapping/packaging that is permeable to steam.
Check and calibrate temperature sensors and pressure gauges regularly.
Perform biological indicator testing (Geobacillus stearothermophilus spore strips) periodically to validate sterilization efficacy.
Wear heat-resistant gloves and face shield when unloading hot materials.
Ensure the safety valve is functional — test as per maintenance schedule.
Keep the area around the autoclave clear of obstruction; mark as a restricted area during operation.
